prompt: A federated engineer authenticates successfully but a Cloud Storage object read is denied after a project move. Diagnose safely.
directAnswer: Bind organization and folder ancestry, project number and ID, principal, token audience without exposing the token, permission, bucket, object, timestamp and audit correlation. Authentication succeeded; authorization did not. Inspect allow policies on the bucket, project, folders and organization; group and principal-set membership; role contents; conditional bindings; deny and principal-access-boundary policies; organization policy; VPC Service Controls if used; uniform bucket-level access; and Cloud Audit Logs. Do not grant Owner. Correct the narrowest reviewed binding or perimeter rule, test the intended read and an intended denial, then record and reconcile the change.
foundation: Google Cloud authorization evaluates a principal, permissions contained in roles, resource ancestry and multiple policy types; authentication alone grants nothing.
reasoningSteps: Bind one denied operation and immutable identifiers.
Walk effective policy from resource to organization.
Separate IAM from organization policy and service perimeter.
Check bucket authorization mode and audit evidence.
seniorAnswer: I preserve the denied request evidence and refuse project-wide Owner because it expands blast radius, hides the actual policy boundary and might not solve a deny or perimeter decision.
weakAnswer: The login works, so download a service-account key and grant Owner on the project.
whyWeak: A new long-lived credential increases risk, Owner is excessive, and deny, bucket, condition, ancestry or perimeter controls may still block the request.

evidence.signal: principal audience permission resource ancestry and audit event

followUps.prompt: What is the core IAM sentence?
followUps.answer: A principal receives a role containing permissions on a resource, subject to inherited and advanced policy controls.

followUps.prompt: Can project Editor guarantee object read?
followUps.answer: Do not assume it; inspect the role permissions, bucket policy, deny controls, access mode and perimeter context.

followUps.prompt: What must never enter incident notes?
followUps.answer: Access tokens, service-account private keys, signed URLs and customer object contents.
